provenance.value: nanosecond (ns); values such as 2262-04-11 15:54:18.854775809 show full ns precision
values near int64 bounds: Timestamp.max._value and Timestamp.min._value; wrap-around of about 585 years; local value landing exactly on the NaT sentinel iNaT

UTC-to-local conversion applies the UTC offset with a bare add, so a UTC instant whose local wall time leaves the int64 range wraps silently and comes back roughly 585 years off; e.g. pd.DatetimeIndex([pd.Timestamp.min], tz="UTC").tz_convert("US/Pacific").tz_localize(None) gives 2262-04-11 15:54:18.854775809 instead of raising. A UTC value of iNaT + 3600*10**9 ns converted to timezone(timedelta(hours=-1)) yields local value == iNaT (which is stored as NaT).

The conversion should raise OutOfBoundsDatetime with message containing 'overflows past' (as the scalar path pd.Timestamp(pd.Timestamp.min._value, tz="UTC").tz_convert("US/Pacific") already does), rather than returning a wrapped value.
